paper_metadata.title: OPIEC: An Open Information Extraction Corpus
paper_metadata.venue: Automated Knowledge Base Construction (2019), Conference paper
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper releases, describes, and profiles OPIEC, a large open-information-extraction corpus derived from English Wikipedia. It contains more than 340 million open triples plus provenance, confidence, syntactic, semantic, spatial, and temporal metadata; comparisons with DBpedia and YAGO examine complementarity to existing knowledge bases.

problem_addressed: The work addresses the lack of a very large, richly annotated open-information-extraction resource for automated knowledge-base construction. It constructs and characterizes a Wikipedia-derived corpus, including cleaner and entity-linked subsets, and tests how its open facts overlap with DBpedia and YAGO. Author contributions: (1) release OPIEC and the OPIEC-Clean and OPIEC-Linked subcorpora; (2) build a scalable extraction pipeline with provenance, confidence, syntactic, factuality, spatial, and temporal metadata; (3) extend MinIE to MinIE-SpaTe; (4) profile corpus quality and analyze alignment/complementarity with DBpedia and YAGO; and (5) release construction code and derived relation-frequency resources.

methodology.description: Execution-order architecture: (1) use a modified WikiExtractor on the 21 June 2017 English Wikipedia dump to produce plain text while preserving internal links as span-to-target annotations, and add a self-link for an article's first exact title mention; (2) run Stanford CoreNLP 3.8.0 for tokenization, sentence splitting, POS tagging, lemmatization, NER, temporal tagging, and dependency parsing; (3) run dependency/clause-based MinIE, based on ClausIE, to generate compact subject–relation–object triples; (4) extend it as MinIE-SpaTe, which transfers polarity, modality, attribution, quantities, and detected temporal/spatial context into annotations, using SUTime, NER, and dependency rules; (5) remove a recurring erroneous NER-type-mismatched “be” pattern, estimate extraction confidence with logistic regression, and repair split Wikipedia links; (6) retain all outputs as OPIEC, then filter clean entity/concept triples for OPIEC-Clean and doubly Wikipedia-linked triples for OPIEC-Linked; and (7) profile corpus characteristics and compare linked facts against DBpedia and YAGO using distant supervision. The method is a corpus-construction and analysis pipeline, rather than a trained end-to-end KG generator.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: No predefined ontology or relation schema constrains OPIEC extraction: it is open IE. Wikipedia page links provide golden entity disambiguation where present; OPIEC-Linked retains triples whose two arguments are linked. DBpedia and YAGO are used after extraction for distant-supervision alignment and comparative profiling, not as an extraction schema. Time is represented in TIMEX3 format.

input_output.input_type: Full unstructured English Wikipedia article text, with retained internal Wikipedia hyperlinks; the appendix evaluation additionally uses sentences from the New York Times corpus.
input_output.input_granularity: Corpus/article-level input is preprocessed and segmented; extraction is performed sentence by sentence. Wikipedia links are retained as document-level span and target-page annotations.
input_output.output_representation: Open subject–relation–object triples with token-level linguistic information and rich attached metadata. OPIEC contains 341.0M triples; OPIEC-Clean contains 104.0M concept/entity-oriented triples; OPIEC-Linked contains 5.8M triples with golden Wikipedia links for both arguments. Metadata includes provenance, POS/lemmas/dependency parse, NER, confidence, polarity, modality, attribution, quantities, space, time, canonical links, and extraction type.

models_and_tools: CoreNLP tokenization, sentence splitting, POS tagging, lemmatization, NER, temporal tagging, and dependency parser
Logistic regression confidence classifier with chi-square feature selection
datasets: English Wikipedia dump of 21 June 2017 (source corpus for OPIEC)
Labelled MinIE datasets from Gashteovski et al. (2017) for the confidence classifier
Independent random sample of 500 OPIEC triples for manual extraction-correctness evaluation
New York Times corpus sample of 10,000 random sentences for spatio-temporal annotation evaluation
DBpedia and YAGO for knowledge-base alignment analysis

metrics: Manual extraction correctness/precision: 355/500 (71%) OPIEC triples correctly extracted
Pearson correlation between confidence score and bucketed precision: r = 0.95
Knowledge-base hit rate: percentage of OPIEC-Linked triples for which DBpedia and/or YAGO contain a triple between the same linked entities
Manual correctness of non-aligned linked triples: 60/100; high-confidence score >0.5 sample: 80/100
Spatio-temporal annotation precision: temporal triple 91/100, temporal argument 80/100, spatial triple 91/100, spatial argument 82/100
baselines: Prior OIE corpora compared descriptively in Table 1: ReVerb, ReVerb-Linked, PATTY (Wiki), WiseNet 2.0, DefIE, and KB-Unify
DBpedia and YAGO are comparative knowledge bases for alignment/overlap analysis, not extraction-model baselines
MinIE without spatio-temporal annotations is the underlying reference extraction in Appendix C's annotation evaluation; only correctly extracted triples are evaluated for annotation correctness
evaluation.setting: The paper evaluates the released corpus rather than reporting a train/test benchmark for a new learned extractor. It profiles full OPIEC and two filtered subsets; manually judges a random independent sample of 500 triples for extraction correctness and calibrates ten equal-width confidence-score buckets; uses gold human-provided Wikipedia links in OPIEC-Linked to align entity pairs against DBpedia/YAGO under a deliberately optimistic distant-supervision KB-hit definition; manually judges two 100-triple non-aligned samples; and evaluates MinIE-SpaTe annotations on four 100-item sets derived from 10,000 New York Times sentences.

value: OPIEC has 341.0M triples, 104.9M unique arguments, and 63.9M unique relations; OPIEC-Clean has 104.0M triples; OPIEC-Linked has 5.8M triples.
About 49% of OPIEC triples carry at least one semantic annotation; 33% have space or time, 19% time, 18% space, and 17% quantities.
The manual OPIEC sample had 71% correct extractions (355/500); confidence scores track precision strongly (Pearson r=0.95).

Only 29.7% of OPIEC-Linked triples have a KB hit in DBpedia or YAGO; thus 70.3% have none under the paper's entity-pair hit definition. Across the 100 most frequent OPIEC-Clean relations, the mean DBpedia hit fraction is 16.8% and the mean number of aligned DBpedia relations is about 42.
For 645,525 linked OPIEC date facts, only 36,262 (5.6%) have an optimistic YAGO date hit. In sampled non-aligned triples, 60% are correct, rising to 80% for a 100-triple sample with score >0.5.
MinIE-SpaTe's manually assessed annotation precision is 91% for triple-level time, 80% for argument-level time, 91% for triple-level space, and 82% for argument-level space.

value: Author-stated/experimental: very large released resource with 341M triples and substantially more metadata than the compared OIE corpora, including provenance, syntactic and semantic annotations, confidence, and retained human-authored Wikipedia links.

Author-stated/experimental: OPIEC-Clean makes a 104M-triple subset more suitable for downstream use by selecting concept/entity-oriented triples; it remains four times larger than the largest prior OIE corpus cited by the authors.
Author-stated/experimental: per-triple confidence is empirically useful, with 71% manual correctness in the 500-triple sample and r=0.95 correlation between score and bucketed precision.
Author-stated/experimental: space/time annotations preserve contextual information with 80–91% precision across the four appendix tests.

[Review inference] This is particularly useful as a Text-to-KG pipeline resource because it preserves provenance, confidence, entity-link evidence, and contextual annotations alongside open triples, enabling later filtering, linking, canonicalization, or validation rather than discarding extraction context.

value: Author-stated/experimental: raw OPIEC contains underspecified triples; 22% of its arguments are personal pronouns, and no anaphora resolution was performed.

Author-stated: raw extractions can be complex, overly specific, or malformed by parsing ambiguities; the full corpus is therefore more suited to research on improving/reasoning with complex OIE than directly to downstream tasks.
Author-stated/experimental: OPIEC does not automatically disambiguate entities; the much smaller OPIEC-Linked subset is only about 5.5% of OPIEC-Clean.

Author-stated/experimental: open relations are highly ambiguous and not directly mappable to KB relations; the top-100 relations average 42 DBpedia alignments, and a KB hit does not guarantee semantic equivalence.

[Review inference] The reported score estimates correctness of extraction rather than factual truth, so downstream KG population still requires fact verification, canonicalization, and relation normalization.

value: No anaphora/coreference resolution is performed; pronoun-, determiner-, and wh-pronoun arguments make many triples under-specified.
Entity mentions, especially works of art that resemble clauses, can yield incorrect extractions; a preliminary study attributes about 1% of OPIEC triples to this issue.
Complex argument phrases are difficult for downstream applications; making triples simpler can lose information.
Automatic entity disambiguation is deliberately not done because automated linkers introduce errors and restrict arguments to confidently linkable ones.
Knowledge-base comparisons are limited by open-relation ambiguity: a KB hit only establishes some relation between the linked entities, not necessarily the same relation or direction.
Spatio-temporal annotation errors arise from incorrect temporal/spatial tags and dependency parses.

value: Author-stated direction: add coreference resolution to resolve underspecified pronoun-based triples and increase usable OIE recall.
Author-stated direction: improve handling/reasoning for complex OIE extractions and complex argument phrases.
Author-stated direction: address entity disambiguation, while balancing the error and coverage trade-off of automatic linkers.
[Review inference] Add relation canonicalization/schema alignment with semantic validation, because entity-pair KB hits are frequently non-equivalent and frequent open relations are polysemous.
[Review inference] Improve temporal/spatial tagging and dependency parsing, then rerun or correct annotations, targeting the concrete error sources reported in Appendix C.

value: Author-stated: robust coreference resolution and interpretation of under-specified OIE triples remain necessary for better OIE recall and downstream use.
Author-stated: disambiguating open triples with respect to a knowledge base is difficult; only entity links are treated as golden in OPIEC-Linked.

Author-stated: determining true semantic equivalence between an open relation and a KB relation remains unresolved; open relations may be generic, specific, correlated, inverse, or semantically different.
Author-stated: harnessing non-aligned OIE facts has both potential and challenges because not all facts are correct and disambiguation is a major challenge.
[Review inference] Converting OPIEC's open triples into a consistently canonical, factually validated knowledge graph is outside this paper's pipeline and remains an end-to-end Text-to-KG problem.
